# gh-shoal

Official source, build, release, and distribution repository for the `gh shoal`
GitHub CLI extension.

## Install

Validation releases are installed through the GitHub CLI extension path with a
pinned release tag:

```bash
gh extension install taco3064/gh-shoal --pin <validation-release-tag>
```

## Build

Build the extension executable from a clean checkout:

```bash
go build -o gh-shoal ./cmd/gh-shoal
```

The installed extension is invoked by GitHub CLI as:

```bash
gh shoal --help
```

## Current CLI surface

The extension includes `gh shoal init` for repair of a direct Personal Account
fork of the canonical Network Root. Run it from a clean local `main` synchronized
with the fork's remote `main`, while authenticated as the fork owner with `gh auth`.
It synchronizes the canonical Issue Form and Summary Workflow, preserves your
`README.md` policy, and commits and pushes only if either managed file changes.
On a fresh fork, the owner must first open the fork's Actions page and confirm
GitHub's workflow enablement prompt. `init` also ensures Issues are enabled and
repairs the GitHub workflow state of the canonical
`.github/workflows/reviewer-summary.yml` if it is inactive. It enables only that
workflow and verifies it is active. `init` does not enable repository-level
Actions or change Actions policy. A successful `init` confirms managed file,
Issues, and canonical workflow-state repair; it does not prove that the manual
Actions confirmation happened or that a workflow run will execute successfully.

Run Automated Review from a clean local Reviewer Node checkout, authenticated as
its Personal Account owner. The canonical Network Root is the root owner's
Reviewer Node; other Reviewers use a direct fork. `gh shoal init` remains a
direct-fork synchronization command and must not run against the Network Root:

```bash
gh shoal review --agent codex
```

Choose one installed Local AI Agent explicitly: `claude`, `codex`, `gemini`,
`opencode`, `cursor`, `grok`, `qwen`, or `kimi`. The extension scans all current
open Issues and applies the admission rules. Invalid requests receive an
explanation and are closed. Valid pending Reviews run in FIFO batches of at
most five. The Agent reads the Reviewer Node's `README.md` policy and writes
its judgments to the ignored temporary `.shoal/review-results.json` file.
The extension then ensures the corresponding Star state, appends a
machine-readable Review Result with the Agent explanation and commit identities,
and closes successfully completed Issues. Failed items remain open for a later
run. The extension does not synchronize your local branch or run Target code.

Run Reviewer-triggered maintenance and pending Re-review work with the same
explicit Local AI Agent contract:

```bash
gh shoal re-review --agent codex
```

`re-review` inspects existing canonical Review Threads, including completed
closed threads and canonical threads already reopened by a valid
`RE_REVIEW_REQUESTED` event. It uses the latest usable Review Judgment as the
prior basis and compares the current Target default-branch HEAD plus the current
`README.md` Review Policy commit. Threads with a changed basis are revalidated
again immediately before semantic judgment and then processed through the same
FIFO batches of at most five and the same Agent result contract as Automated
Review. A successful semantic Re-review records the Protocol-defined Judgment
type using the judgment-start Target and Policy commits: PASS records
`RE_REVIEWED`, while FAIL that revokes the endorsement records `STAR_REVOKED`.

When the Review Basis has not changed, `re-review` does not ask the Agent for a
new judgment. Instead, it verifies endorsement state against the latest usable
Judgment: a missing Star after PASS is restored, and a present Star after FAIL is
removed. This deterministic maintenance does not create a new semantic Review
Event. A closed thread with no usable prior Judgment is skipped rather than
reconstructed, and malformed older comments do not override a newer valid
Judgment. Target repositories are identified by stable GitHub Repository ID and
are not executed during discovery, classification, or maintenance.

The machine-readable request and event contract comes from
[`shoal-app/protocol/review-v1.json`](https://github.com/taco3064/shoal-app/blob/main/protocol/review-v1.json).
Its checked-in embedded copy at `internal/cli/protocol/review-v1.json` must remain
byte-identical to the approved platform contract.

## Compatibility, migration, and recovery

The installed binary uses a generated capability snapshot of the exact reviewed
Platform source at `c9d585a06449b5cd38acbf6c4b5590419938b1ce` (tree
`baadeeac21142ab9c5a184cb2e970fececc6a2eb`). The snapshot includes the exact
Protocol bytes and the Platform's explicit managed-surface / Summary contract
bindings. CI and release verification compare committed Platform bytes and
regenerate the snapshot. Updating a component version does not expand Protocol
support; mutable runtime discovery never expands an installed binary's authority.

Review commands check the remote default-branch managed surfaces at one exact
commit and scan formal history before admission, Agent execution, or lifecycle
mutation. Older explicitly supported official station generations can still be
reviewed. An explicit `init` nevertheless synchronizes to the current verified
Network Root, provided that generation is within the installed capability. It
never changes `README.md` or historical comments.

| Diagnostic | Safe next action |
| --- | --- |
| `SUPPORTED` | Existing Review lifecycle rules apply. |
| `REPAIRABLE_STATION_DRIFT` | Run `gh shoal init` from synchronized main; Root owners repair canonical surfaces through maintainer work. |
| `CLI_UPGRADE_REQUIRED` | Upgrade the official Extension before retrying. |
| `INCOMPATIBLE_PROTOCOL_EVIDENCE` | Inspect unsupported formal evidence; this binary will not reinterpret or rewrite it. |
| `EXTERNAL_STATE_UNAVAILABLE` | Restore observable external state before retrying; inspect ambiguous writes rather than blindly repeating them. |
| `NO_CHANGES` | Successful no-op; no synthetic mutation is needed. |

Lost write acknowledgements are followed by bounded authoritative reads. An
exact owner-authored comment or verified converged Star / Issue / settings state
can complete recovery. Unknown state never authorizes a second blind write.
A completed Judgment followed by a failed close is recognized on retry without
another semantic Judgment. Failed `init` pushes retain local rollback behavior;
reconcile the observable remote main before retrying if the remote may have
accepted the push.

Reproduce source correspondence and installed-command smoke with Node 24, Go,
and GitHub CLI available:

```bash
node script/compatibility.mjs <exact-shoal-app-checkout>
go test ./...
node script/smoke-compatibility.mjs
```

The smoke uses an isolated GitHub CLI installation, native local Git transport,
and controlled GitHub / Agent responses. It performs no real Review, Star,
workflow, or repository-setting writes.

## Release

Release publication is owned by this repository through
`.github/workflows/release.yml`.

Pull request validation proves release readiness without creating a real tag or
GitHub Release. It builds the full asset matrix, checks release workflow
configuration, runs native smoke checks, installs the current checkout through
GitHub CLI's local extension path, and verifies:

```bash
gh extension install .
gh shoal --help
```

Normal release publication happens only after merge. Tag the intended `main`
commit to publish precompiled GitHub CLI extension assets:

```bash
git switch main
git pull --ff-only origin main
git tag v0.1.0
git push origin v0.1.0
```

The release tag must point at the exact `main` commit intended for publication.
PR-stage tags and PR-stage GitHub Releases are not part of the normal release
lifecycle.

The release workflow builds this initial matrix:

- Linux amd64
- Linux arm64
- macOS / Darwin amd64
- macOS / Darwin arm64
- Windows amd64
- Windows arm64

Artifact Attestations are generated for the published executables so users can
verify the relationship between the `gh-shoal` repository, release workflow,
source commit, and released binary.

After the release workflow completes, verify the published assets, attestations,
and remote installation before closing the release-foundation issue:

```bash
gh release download <validation-release-tag> \
  --repo taco3064/gh-shoal \
  --pattern "gh-shoal-*"

for asset in gh-shoal-*; do
  gh attestation verify "$asset" --repo taco3064/gh-shoal
done

gh extension install taco3064/gh-shoal --pin <validation-release-tag>
gh shoal --help
```

The post-merge release gate verifies distribution mechanics: tag selection,
release publication, asset upload, digest, attestation, and remote asset
resolution. It is not a substitute for PR-stage runtime testing. If the remote
install resolves but `gh shoal --help` crashes or exposes behavior that the PR
exact-head local-install gate should have caught, treat that as a PR validation
escape and tighten PR CI before closing the release-foundation issue.

name: ci

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  test:
    name: test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}

      - name: Verify exact candidate head
        shell: bash
        run: test "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = "${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}"

      - name: Setup Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@v7
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod

      - name: Setup Node for compatibility verification
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'

      - name: Checkout exact compatibility authority
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          repository: taco3064/shoal-app
          ref: c9d585a06449b5cd38acbf6c4b5590419938b1ce
          path: compatibility-source

      - name: Verify exact Platform correspondence
        run: node script/compatibility.mjs compatibility-source

      - name: Test
        run: go test ./...

      - name: Build extension executable
        run: go build -o gh-shoal ./cmd/gh-shoal

      - name: Smoke root help
        run: ./gh-shoal --help

  release-readiness:
    name: release readiness
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}

      - name: Verify exact candidate head
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          expected="${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}"
          actual="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
          test "$actual" = "$expected"

      - name: Setup Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@v7
        with:
          go-version-file: go.mod

      - name: Setup Node for compatibility verification
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'

      - name: Checkout exact compatibility authority
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          repository: taco3064/shoal-app
          ref: c9d585a06449b5cd38acbf6c4b5590419938b1ce
          path: compatibility-source

      - name: Verify exact Platform correspondence
        run: node script/compatibility.mjs compatibility-source

      - name: Verify release workflow configuration
        run: bash script/verify-release-workflow.sh

      - name: Build release asset matrix
        run: script/build-release.sh v0.0.0-ci

      - name: Verify expected release assets
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          test -x dist/gh-shoal-linux-amd64
          test -x dist/gh-shoal-linux-arm64
          test -x dist/gh-shoal-darwin-amd64
          test -x dist/gh-shoal-darwin-arm64
          test -f dist/gh-shoal-windows-amd64.exe
          test -f dist/gh-shoal-windows-arm64.exe

      - name: Smoke Linux amd64 release binary
        run: ./dist/gh-shoal-linux-amd64 --help

  local-extension-install:
    name: local extension install (${{ matrix.os }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            binary: gh-shoal
          - os: macos-latest
            binary: gh-shoal
          - os: windows-latest
            binary: gh-shoal.exe
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
          path: gh-shoal

      - name: Verify exact candidate head
        working-directory: gh-shoal
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          expected="${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}"
          actual="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
          test "$actual" = "$expected"

      - name: Setup Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@v7
        with:
          go-version-file: gh-shoal/go.mod

      - name: Build native executable
        working-directory: gh-shoal
        run: go build -o ${{ matrix.binary }} ./cmd/gh-shoal

      - name: Smoke root help
        working-directory: gh-shoal
        run: ./${{ matrix.binary }} --help

      - name: Setup Node for installed command smoke
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'

      - name: Exact-head unit and integration verification
        working-directory: gh-shoal
        run: go test ./...

      - name: Installed-extension compatibility and recovery smoke
        working-directory: gh-shoal
        run: node script/smoke-compatibility.mjs

name: release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*"

permissions:
  contents: write
  id-token: write
  attestations: write

jobs:
  release:
    name: publish precompiled extension
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout release source
        uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - name: Setup Node for compatibility verification
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '24'

      - name: Checkout exact compatibility authority
        uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          repository: taco3064/shoal-app
          ref: c9d585a06449b5cd38acbf6c4b5590419938b1ce
          path: compatibility-source

      - name: Verify exact Platform correspondence
        run: node script/compatibility.mjs compatibility-source

      - name: Publish GitHub CLI extension release
        uses: cli/gh-extension-precompile@v2.2.0
        with:
          go_version_file: go.mod
          build_script_override: script/build-release.sh
          generate_attestations: true

issues.title: [Phase 1 · 06] Implement the Automated Review MVP
issues.body:
## Roadmap status

**Shaped — delivery-ready.**

This issue is the delivery contract for Shoal milestone [06]. Delivery may choose internal module structure and adapter implementation details, but must preserve the Product BR, the shaped admission contract from milestone [05], the Automated Review responsibility boundary, and the observable behavior defined below.

## Goal

Implement the first complete Reviewer-side Automated Review path in `gh-shoal`.

A single Reviewer invocation must:

- require an explicit Local AI Agent choice;
- scan the current Reviewer Node's open Issues;
- rerun deterministic Review Request admission for each open Issue;
- reject and close invalid requests using the admission behavior shaped in [05];
- collect valid pending Review Threads in FIFO order;
- review them in batches of at most five;
- invoke the selected Local AI Agent with the canonical Review instructions;
- receive structured batch results through a temporary JSON contract;
- apply the resulting PASS / FAIL GitHub Star state;
- append a protocol-valid Review Result comment;
- close each successfully completed Review Thread;
- complete the Phase 1 `gh-shoal` delivery by publishing the accepted merged implementation as `v0.1.0`.

The Local AI Agent is the semantic judge. `gh-shoal` remains the deterministic protocol executor and the owner of GitHub mutations.

This milestone is also the Phase 1 release owner for `gh-shoal`. Functional correctness must be proven on the pull-request candidate before merge. The post-merge `v0.1.0` release step verifies distribution only; `main` is not a fallback runtime testing surface.

## Primary repository

- `gh-shoal`

## Protocol authority

- `shoal-app`

## Affected repository

- `shoal-station`

## Depends on

- [05] Establish the Review Request, admission, and Review Thread lifecycle: https://github.com/taco3064/gh-shoal/issues/4

## Evidence

The Product BR defines:

```text
Reviewer
= Review Policy Owner

README.md
= Review Policy

AI Agent
= Authorized Semantic Judge

Core / gh Extension
= Deterministic Protocol Executor
```

The Product BR also defines the official Automated Review path as Reviewer-triggered local execution. There is no hosted or background Shoal reviewer.

Milestone [05] already shapes the deterministic Request admission and canonical Review Thread lifecycle. This milestone starts from that contract and adds semantic judgment plus the resulting Star / Unstar and completed Review Event behavior.

## Product / Protocol Decisions

### 1. Command contract

Automated Review is invoked as:

```bash
gh shoal review --agent <agent>
```

`--agent` is required.

Shoal must not auto-detect, silently select, or fall back to another Local AI Agent.

The user-facing value is the Agent / product name rather than an executable path.

Initial supported values are:

```text
claude
codex
gemini
opencode
cursor
grok
qwen
kimi
```

The adapter layer owns the mapping from those values to the corresponding Local AI Agent CLI invocation.

Unsupported Agent values fail explicitly.

Arbitrary executable paths are not part of the MVP Agent contract.

### 2. Run-level Station precondition

Automated Review may run only when the current Reviewer Node / Station working tree is clean.

The run must abort before Issue processing, Agent invocation, or Review side effects when the Station contains uncommitted working-tree changes.

Ignored runtime files under the Station's ignore policy do not make the Station dirty.

Shoal does not manage or validate the user's Git branch strategy or local-versus-remote synchronization state.

In particular, Shoal does not:

- require local HEAD to equal the remote default branch;
- auto-fetch;
- auto-pull;
- auto-rebase;
- auto-merge.

The Review Result records the Review Policy commit version and Target commit hash, so repository-state provenance is carried by the Review record rather than by enforcing the user's Git workflow.

### 3. Every run scans all current open Issues

`gh shoal review` does not take an Issue number.

Each invocation scans the current Reviewer Node's open Issues and reruns deterministic admission.

For every open Issue:

```text
open Issue
→ admission validation
```

Invalid requests follow the milestone [05] admission contract:

```text
deterministic rejection reason
→ fixed explanatory comment
→ close Issue
→ do not enter semantic Review
```

The Station Issue surface is reserved for Review Requests. An open Issue that does not satisfy the Review Request contract is therefore handled as an invalid request rather than preserved as a general-purpose Issue.

An Issue that remains open because an earlier Agent or side-effect attempt failed is eligible to be processed again on the next `gh shoal review` invocation.

### 4. Valid pending Reviews are FIFO

After admission, valid pending Review Threads are ordered by Issue number ascending.

Older requests are processed before newer requests.

No additional queue state is required.

### 5. Review batch size is five

Valid pending Review Threads are processed in batches of at most five.

```text
valid pending Review Threads
→ Issue number ascending
→ batches of max 5
→ one Local AI Agent process per batch
```

A run with more than five valid pending requests continues through subsequent batches until the current run's work is exhausted.

Each repository remains an independent Review judgment even when multiple requests are passed to the same Agent batch.

### 6. Agent input starts from the Review Request Issue URL

For each batch, `gh-shoal` gives the selected Agent the Review Request Issue URLs and instructions for resolving each Target Repository from the Issue contract.

Shoal does not clone Target Repositories into the user's machine for Automated Review.

The Agent is expected to inspect the relevant GitHub repository state through the tools and capabilities available to that Agent.

The prompt must explicitly state that the Reviewer Node's `README.md` contains the authoritative Review Policy and must be read before judgment.

The prompt must communicate the equivalent of:

```text
The Review criteria are defined in this Reviewer Node's README.md.
Read README.md first and use it as the authoritative Review Policy.
```

### 7. Agent GitHub mutation is forbidden

The Local AI Agent performs semantic inspection and judgment only.

The canonical Review prompt must explicitly forbid the Agent from:

- commenting on the Review Issue;
- closing the Review Issue;
- starring a repository;
- unstarring a repository;
- creating or mutating other GitHub state as part of the Review result.

The Agent may:

- read the Review Request;
- resolve the Target Repository;
- read the Reviewer Node `README.md` Review Policy;
- inspect the Target Repository and relevant evidence;
- decide PASS or FAIL;
- write the structured result to the provided temporary JSON file.

All Shoal Review mutations remain owned by `gh-shoal`.

### 8. Temporary JSON is the Agent-to-CLI result contract

The authoritative Agent result is not stdout or stderr.

Each Agent batch writes its structured result to:

```text
.shoal/review-results.json
```

inside the current Station working tree.

stdout / stderr are execution logs only and are not parsed as the formal Review result.

The CLI owns creation and cleanup of the temporary runtime file.

The temporary file is deleted after the batch result is consumed.

The Station ignore policy must ensure `.shoal/` is not tracked.

Each result contains at least:

```json
{
  "issue": 12,
  "verdict": "PASS",
  "comment": "Repository-specific review explanation"
}
```

Allowed verdicts are:

```text
PASS
FAIL
```

The Agent result contains semantic judgment only. Protocol metadata is resolved by `gh-shoal`.

### 9. Partial batch results are valid

Batch processing is per Review Thread, not transactional.

If a batch contains five valid pending Reviews and the Agent produces valid results for only four:

- the four valid results continue through normal side effects;
- the missing or unusable result remains open;
- the missing result does not roll back completed siblings;
- the CLI reports the failed / missing item locally;
- the open Issue may be retried by a later `gh shoal review` run.

An Agent execution failure is not a Review FAIL.

### 10. Review explanation remains Agent-authored

The Agent produces the repository-specific Review explanation.

`gh-shoal` must not replace it with a generic semantic summary.

The canonical prompt must require the Review explanation to remain concise and human-readable and must instruct the Agent:

```text
Keep the review explanation concise and readable.
The review explanation must not exceed 3,000 characters.
Focus on the decisive evidence and reasoning.
```

The 3,000-character requirement is an Agent prompt constraint. The CLI does not independently reject or truncate a result merely because the Agent slightly exceeds that requested size.

### 11. Review Result comment st

comments.body:
Shape decision: Local AI Agent selection and supported values

The Automated Review CLI contract is:

```text
gh shoal review --agent <agent>
```

Decisions:

- `--agent` is required.
- Shoal must not auto-detect or silently choose an Agent.
- The user-facing value is the Agent / product name, not the executable name.
- The adapter layer owns mapping from the selected value to the actual CLI command.
- Initial supported values:
  - `claude`
  - `codex`
  - `gemini`
  - `opencode`
  - `cursor`
  - `grok`
  - `qwen`
  - `kimi`
- Unsupported values must fail explicitly.
- Shoal should not accept arbitrary executable paths as a substitute for the supported Agent contract.
- The public website must document the same user-facing Agent choices, while `gh-shoal` remains the executable implementation authority.

Shape decision: temporary review result file

- Each Agent batch writes its structured result to:
  `.shoal/review-results.json`
  inside the current Reviewer Node / station working tree.
- The result file is temporary runtime state and must never be committed.
- The station repository is expected to ignore everything except its canonical tracked surfaces, so `.shoal/` remains ignored by default.
- The CLI owns creation/cleanup of the temporary result file and deletes it after consuming the batch result.
- JSON is the authoritative Agent-to-CLI review result contract; stdout/stderr are execution logs only.

Shape decision: clean Station precondition

Automated Review may run only when the current Reviewer Node / station working tree is completely clean.

Before scanning or reviewing Issues, `gh shoal review` must verify there are no tracked or untracked working-tree changes that would make the local Station state ambiguous. If the Station is dirty, abort the review run before invoking any Local AI Agent or performing any GitHub review side effect.

This is a run-level precondition, not a README-only check. Ignored runtime files such as `.shoal/review-results.json` are excluded from this cleanliness requirement by the Station's ignore policy.

Phase 1 delivery complete.

Final release / distribution gate:

- Merged main commit: `5440c40eeee82831d18742251d603fc992d383fa`
- Release tag: `v0.1.0`, verified against that exact commit
- Main CI: run `35954802484` — success
- Release workflow: run `35955094825` — success
- Published release contains the complete six-binary matrix for Linux/macOS/Windows × amd64/arm64
- Downloaded asset SHA-256 values match the release API digests
- Artifact Attestation verification succeeded for every published binary and bound each asset to the expected `gh-shoal` repository, `.github/workflows/release.yml`, source commit, and `refs/tags/v0.1.0`
- The workflow-created draft Release was explicitly published by the repository owner
- Public distribution verification was then performed as `taco-gem` in an isolated GitHub CLI environment
- `gh extension install taco3064/gh-shoal --pin v0.1.0` succeeded
- The installed Extension reports `gh shoal v0.1.0`
- `gh shoal --help` succeeds and exposes the shipped `init` and `review` command surfaces
- Installed Windows amd64 binary digest matches the verified release asset
- Distribution verification did not mutate Review Requests or Star state

The post-merge gate remained distribution-only; functional/runtime validation had already been completed and approved on PR #10 exact head before merge.

All acceptance and release gates for #3 are satisfied. Closing this issue completes the Phase 1 `gh-shoal` delivery.

issues.title: [Phase 1 · 07] Establish Review maintenance and automated/manual convergence
issues.body:
## Roadmap status

**Shaped — delivery-ready.**

This issue is the delivery contract for Shoal milestone [07].

It owns the complete `gh-shoal` runtime behavior for Review maintenance, Automated Re-review, endorsement-state reconciliation, and Automated / Manual observable convergence. Delivery may choose implementation details that fit the current repository, but must preserve the current Product BR, the completed [05] / [06] behavior, the Review Protocol already consumed by `gh-shoal`, and the observable contract below.

## Goal

Extend the shipped Automated Review runtime so a Reviewer can maintain existing Review-backed endorsements through:

```bash
gh shoal re-review --agent <agent>
```

The command must:

- discover existing Review lifecycles that require maintenance;
- recognize both Reviewer-triggered closed-thread maintenance and requester-triggered pending Re-review lifecycles;
- compare the latest usable Review Judgment with the current Review Basis and Actual GitHub Star State;
- invoke semantic Re-review only when a new Review Basis still exists at judgment start;
- reuse the existing Automated Review Agent / batching / result / side-effect pipeline rather than creating a second review engine;
- reconcile endorsement drift deterministically without unnecessary semantic judgment;
- append Protocol-valid Re-review Judgment Events and converge the canonical Review Thread to the correct completed / retryable state;
- preserve Manual Review / Re-review as a legitimate path producing the same Protocol-valid observable outcome;
- skip unverifiable historical state without reconstructing or guessing history and without blocking independent work;
- prove the exact PR-head Re-review lifecycle through the installed Extension path before merge;
- complete Phase 1 Extension distribution after merge so the official remotely installable release includes `gh shoal re-review`.

## Primary repository

- `gh-shoal`

## Depends on

- [Phase 1 · 05] Establish the Review Request, admission, and Review Thread lifecycle: https://github.com/taco3064/gh-shoal/issues/4
- [Phase 1 · 06] Implement the Automated Review MVP: https://github.com/taco3064/gh-shoal/issues/3

## Evidence

The current Product BR defines the public gh Extension surface as:

```text
gh shoal init
gh shoal review
gh shoal re-review
```

and defines Re-review maintenance as:

```text
discover closed canonical Review Threads
+ compare current Review Basis
+ detect endorsement drift
+ semantic re-review only when Review Basis changed
```

The completed [05] admission / lifecycle milestone already provides:

- one canonical Review Thread per Reviewer Node Repository ID + Target Repository ID;
- `NO_NEW_REVIEW_BASIS` handling for duplicate request triggers;
- `RE_REVIEW_REQUESTED` lifecycle events;
- reopen of the existing canonical Review Thread for an admitted requester-triggered Re-review;
- stable Reviewer Node / Target Repository identity handling.

The completed [06] Automated Review milestone already provides:

- required `--agent <agent>` selection;
- supported Local AI Agent adapters;
- one Agent process per batch of at most five;
- Issue-number ordering;
- `.shoal/review-results.json` as the Agent result contract;
- per-thread partial success / failure isolation;
- Agent-owned semantic PASS / FAIL;
- `gh-shoal`-owned GitHub mutations;
- judgment-start Target / Policy snapshotting;
- Star / Unstar convergence before the completed Review Judgment Event;
- retryable execution failure rather than semantic FAIL.

Current `gh-shoal` repository reality also already includes the Review Protocol contract and validation used by Initial Review. Re-review must extend that runtime, not fork a separate protocol interpretation.

The current published validation release `v0.1.0` points to commit `5440c40eeee82831d18742251d603fc992d383fa`, which is the repository state immediately before this milestone. Because this milestone is now the final Phase 1 gh Extension feature milestone, its delivery contract must also prove the Re-review runtime from the exact PR head and publish a later validation release after merge so the official distribution contains the completed Phase 1 command surface.

## Product / Protocol Decisions

### 1. Public command contract

Automated maintenance is invoked as:

```bash
gh shoal re-review --agent <agent>
```

`--agent` is required and uses the same supported Agent contract as:

```bash
gh shoal review --agent <agent>
```

Shoal must not:

- auto-detect or silently select an Agent;
- introduce a different Agent list for Re-review;
- reintroduce public `stale` or `status` commands;
- require an Issue number as the normal Re-review product interface.

### 2. Reviewer Node execution authority

`gh shoal re-review` must run only against a Reviewer Node owned by the authenticated Reviewer that satisfies the current Product BR Reviewer Node membership rule:

```text
repository is a fork
+ repository owner is a Personal Account
+ reviewerNode.parent.id === NETWORK_ROOT_REPOSITORY_ID
```

`repository.source.id` is not Reviewer Node Membership authority.

Reuse the same authenticated Reviewer Node resolution already established by the delivered Review runtime.

### 3. Two Re-review candidate sources converge on one lifecycle

Re-review has two legitimate entry paths.

#### Reviewer-triggered maintenance

When the Reviewer explicitly runs:

```bash
gh shoal re-review --agent <agent>
```

the CLI discovers existing **closed canonical Review Threads**.

For each discovered thread it resolves:

```text
latest usable Review Judgment
current Target default-branch HEAD
current Review Policy Commit
Actual GitHub Star State
```

and classifies Review Basis / endorsement state.

#### Requester-triggered maintenance

A later valid Request Trigger may already have been admitted by [05]:

```text
changed Review Basis
→ append RE_REVIEW_REQUESTED
→ reopen existing canonical Review Thread
→ close trigger and redirect to canonical thread
```

`gh shoal re-review` must also recognize and consume these already-reopened canonical Review Threads carrying a valid pending `RE_REVIEW_REQUESTED` lifecycle state.

A reopened pending Re-review Thread must not:

- become stranded because it is open rather than closed;
- be treated as a new Initial Review Request;
- be sent through Initial Review admission again.

Both entry paths converge on the same canonical Review lifecycle and the same semantic Re-review execution path.

### 4. Review Basis classification

The latest usable prior Review Judgment provides:

```text
Previous Target Commit
Previous Review Policy Commit
```

The current observation provides:

```text
Current Target default-branch HEAD
Current Review Policy Commit
```

Classify:

```text
Target changed only
→ TARGET_CHANGED

Policy changed only
→ POLICY_CHANGED

Both changed
→ TARGET_AND_POLICY_CHANGED

Neither changed
→ NO_NEW_REVIEW_BASIS
```

Only changed-basis cases are eligible to proceed toward semantic Re-review.

### 5. Judgment-start revalidation is mandatory

Eligibility observation is not the final Review Judgment snapshot.

Immediately before semantic Re-review begins, resolve again:

```text
Target Commit SHA
= Target Repository default-branch HEAD at judgment start

Review Policy Commit SHA
= README.md last-modifying commit at judgment start
```

Then compare that judgment-start basis with the previous usable Review Judgment.

If the basis has returned to the previous Review Basis while waiting:

```text
NO_NEW_REVIEW_BASIS
→ do not invoke the Agent
→ do not create a Re-review Judgment
→ return the canonical Review Thread to completed / closed state
```

A completed Re-review Judgment Event records the judgment-start snapshot, not the earlier eligibility snapshot.

### 6. Re-review reuses the Automated Review execution pipeline

Once a thread is eligible for semantic Re-review, reuse the [06] execution model:

```text
eligible pending Re-review Threads
→ Issue number ascending
→ batches of max 5
→ one Local AI Agent process per batch
```

Reuse the same:

- Agent adapter contract;
- prompt safety boundary;
- temporary structured result path;
- PASS / FAIL authority;
- explanation ownership;
- per-thread partial result handling;
- GitHub mutation ownership;
- failure isolation;
- retry model.

Do not implement a second semantic review engine merely because the event type is Re-review.

### 7. Agent authority remains semantic only

The Local AI Agent may inspect evidence and return one semantic result per requested thread.

It must not:

- comment on GitHub Issues;
- close or reopen Issues;
- Star / Unstar repositories;
- mutate other GitHub state as part of the result.

`gh-shoal` remains responsible for deterministic Protocol metadata and all Review-result GitHub mutations.

### 8. Re-review Judgment Event

A successful semantic Re-review appends a Protocol-valid machine-readable Review Judgment Event to the canonical Review Thread using the current Re-review e

issues.body:
## Roadmap status

**Shaped — delivery-ready.**

This issue is the `gh-shoal` Phase 2 contract for compatibility-aware local execution, direct-fork migration, diagnostics, and failure-safe recovery.

It consumes the Product BR-backed compatibility authority owned by `shoal-app` and the canonical station generations owned by `shoal-station`. It must not create a second compatibility authority inside the Extension.

## Goal

Make `gh shoal init`, `gh shoal review`, and `gh shoal re-review` deterministic when the installed Extension, the Reviewer Node managed surfaces, and the public Shoal Protocol evidence are not all on the same generation.

The observable model must be:

```text
installed gh-shoal
+ explicit supported Protocol/schema contract snapshot
+ current Reviewer Node state
+ current canonical Network Root state when init needs it
↓
classify before side effects
↓
supported
| repairable station drift
| CLI upgrade required
| incompatible Protocol evidence
| required external state unavailable
| ordinary no-op
```

and then:

```text
supported review/re-review state
→ execute existing Phase 1 lifecycle semantics

repairable direct-fork station state
→ gh shoal init may synchronize only Shoal-managed station surfaces

unsupported / unknown / unverifiable state
→ fail closed before unsafe mutation or semantic judgment
```

The work must preserve Reviewer-owned Review Policy, existing Reviewer Node identity / Membership rules, the Phase 1 Review and Re-review lifecycle, and exact GitHub-side evidence semantics.

## Dependencies / ownership alignment

This ticket is Phase 2 · 04 and consumes the completed contracts produced by:

- `shoal-app#23` — Protocol / schema compatibility and Network trust convergence;
- `shoal-action#4` — Marketplace Action distribution trust and compatibility handoff;
- `shoal-station#9` — canonical managed-surface evolution and immutable Reviewer Summary recovery.

Delivery must use the final delivered identities / contracts from those work items. It must not guess their final digests, Action SHAs, generated artifacts, or compatibility entries from this Issue.

Ownership remains:

```text
shoal-app
= Product / Protocol source SSOT
+ explicit compatibility authority

shoal-station
= current canonical managed-surface bytes
+ canonical Summary Workflow runtime

shoal-action
= Marketplace Action distribution
+ exact distribution provenance

gh-shoal
= local Reviewer execution
+ direct-fork synchronization / migration
+ compatibility-aware local diagnostics / refusal
+ Extension release / distribution
```

## Evidence

### Product BR

The current Product BR v0.63 establishes the following constraints relevant to this ticket:

- Product component versions and Protocol versions are independent.
- Compatibility is governed by explicit `protocolVersion` and governed schema contracts, not by Extension / Action / Website semantic versions.
- Official managed-surface compatibility may include multiple exact canonical digests at the same time.
- Exact managed-surface bytes are identity; semantic equivalence and normalization are not compatibility authority.
- `README.md` is Reviewer-owned Review Policy and must never be rewritten by `gh shoal init`.
- The only `init` repository-content mutation paths are:
  - `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/review-request.yml`
  - `.github/workflows/reviewer-summary.yml`
- `gh shoal init` obtains canonical managed-file bytes from the verified Network Root and remains a direct-fork synchronization operation; it is not a Network Root self-synchronization path.
- Reviewer Node Membership and identity remain GitHub-native stable-ID decisions and are independent from managed-surface compatibility.
- `review` and `re-review` are the public Automated Review / maintenance commands. No new public `status` or `stale` command is implied by version-aware diagnostics.
- Unknown or unsupported Protocol evidence must not be treated as trusted current evidence.

### Current `gh-shoal` implementation

The current repository already provides:

- `gh shoal init` direct-fork validation, exact Network Root snapshot fetch, two-file managed synchronization, clean-tree checks, commit/push rollback, Issues enablement, and canonical workflow activation repair;
- `gh shoal review` deterministic admission, batching, Local AI Agent execution, Star convergence, Review Event append, and completed-thread retry behavior;
- `gh shoal re-review` Review Basis comparison, endorsement-state reconciliation, semantic Re-review, and retry-safe handling of completed judgments;
- an embedded `internal/cli/protocol/review-v1.json` copy that is documented as byte-identical to the Platform Protocol contract;
- exact-head PR CI, local GitHub CLI extension installation smoke coverage, release asset construction, and attested binary publication.

The current embedded review contract exposes `protocolVersion: "1"`. It does not establish a general Phase 2 compatibility registry by itself.

### Current `shoal-app` implementation direction

The current Platform compatibility surface already owns Network Root identity, managed-surface paths, allowed Request Form digests, and canonical Summary Workflow digest → pinned Action identity.

`shoal-app#23` explicitly owns convergence of those primitives with the supported Protocol/schema contract.

Therefore this ticket must consume that delivered authority rather than independently deciding which Protocol/schema/workflow generations are supported.

## Product / Protocol Decisions

### 1. `gh-shoal` consumes compatibility authority; it does not define it

The Extension must have a deterministic local representation of the compatibility contract it is capable of executing.

That representation MUST originate from an exact reviewed `shoal-app` compatibility source candidate.

It may be embedded, generated, or checked in within `gh-shoal`, but CI / release verification must prove exact correspondence to the selected authoritative `shoal-app` source / compatibility artifact.

It MUST NOT be maintained as an independently edited second matrix.

Do not infer support from:

- `gh-shoal` semantic version;
- `shoal-action` semantic version;
- numeric Protocol ordering;
- same-major-version assumptions;
- mutable branches or `latest` tags;
- schema structural similarity;
- YAML semantic equivalence;
- Network Root file age.

An unknown contract is unsupported until the Platform compatibility authority explicitly supports it and a `gh-shoal` release explicitly consumes that supported contract.

### 2. Runtime must use the installed Extension's proven capability snapshot

A running Extension must decide using the compatibility snapshot shipped with that exact Extension candidate.

It must not silently expand its execution authority by trusting a newer mutable compatibility definition fetched at runtime.

A live `shoal-app` read may be used for diagnostics or explicit upgrade discovery if Delivery can prove its identity, but it MUST NOT make an old binary capable of executing a Protocol/schema generation that the binary was not built and tested to support.

This separates:

```text
Platform compatibility truth
= what Shoal currently approves

installed Extension capability
= approved contract generations this exact binary is proven to execute
```

If Platform truth has advanced beyond the installed Extension capability, the correct local result is `CLI upgrade required`, not speculative execution.

### 3. Managed-surface compatibility and `init` synchronization are different decisions

A direct-fork Reviewer Node may contain an older official managed-surface generation that is still explicitly supported.

Therefore:

```text
supported older managed surface
≠ incompatible Reviewer Node
≠ automatic review refusal
```

`review` and `re-review` may execute when the Reviewer Node's required managed surfaces are within the installed Extension's explicit supported compatibility set and all other command preconditions pass.

However, when the Reviewer explicitly runs:

```bash
gh shoal init
```

the command remains the canonical direct-fork synchronization path and targets the current verified Network Root managed bytes.

So:

```text
compatibility
= may this generation safely participate?

init synchronization
= should this direct fork converge to the current canonical Network Root bytes?
```

These MUST NOT be collapsed into one rule.

### 4. `init` must prove the target generation is executable before mutation

Before any `init` side effect, including repository-content writes, Issues enablement, or workflow activation, the command must:

1. validate the direct-fork Reviewer Node and authenticated owner;
2. resolve one exact current Network Root snapshot;
3. obtain both managed files from that snapshot;
4. calculate / validate their exact identities;
5. prove that the target managed-surface generation is supported by the installed Extension capability snapshot.
